Q98.subtopic: Isomeric C8H11N Amines via Gabriel Synthesis
Q98.conceptHtml: Gabriel synthesis yields 1° amines with −NH<sub>2</sub> on an sp3 carbon (no arylamines).
Q98.stepsHtml:
1. Step 1 — Apply the Gabriel phthalimide restriction: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis uses an $S_N2$ reaction with potassium phthalimide, so it can only form primary ($1^\circ$) aralkyl amines where $-\text{NH}_2$ is attached to an $sp^3$ side-chain carbon (aryl halides do not undergo $S_N2$).
  2. Step 2 — Count monosubstituted benzene isomers ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{NH}_2$): (1) 2-Phenylethanamine ($\text{Ph}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, achiral: $1$ isomer). (2) 1-Phenylethanamine ($\text{Ph}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{NH}_2$), which has a chiral carbon and exists as a pair of $(R)$ and $(S)$ enantiomers ($2$ stereoisomers).
  3. Step 3 — Count disubstituted benzene isomers ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$): Placing $-\text{CH}_3$ and $-\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ on the ring gives three positional isomers: ortho-, meta-, and para-methylbenzylamine ($3$ isomers).
  4. Step 4 — Final confirmation: Summing all isomers gives $1 + 2 + 3 = \mathbf{6}$ isomeric aromatic amines.

trapCards.title: Trap 1: Gabriel vs Hoffmann Scope & Stoichiome- try
trapCards.html:
• Gabriel Phthalimide: Works ONLY for 1◦ aliphatic/benzylic amines (PhCH2NH2). NEVER gives aniline or p-toluidine because Ar − X resists SN2.
  • Hoffmann Bromamide: Consumes 4 mol NaOH + 1 mol Br2 (not 2 mol Br2!). Works for both alkyl and aryl 1◦ amides, giving 1 carbon less. Fails for 2◦ amides.
  • Acetylation Mass Gain: Each −NH2 → −NHCOCH3 adds 42 g/mol (not 43).

trapCards.title: Trap 2: Aqueous Basicity & pK<sub>b</sub> Reversals
trapCards.html:
• Gas Phase: Always 3◦ > 2◦ > 1◦ > NH3.
  • Aqueous Methyl vs Ethyl: – Me2NH > MeNH2 > Me3N > NH3 (2◦ > 1◦ > 3◦). – Et2NH > Et3N > EtNH2 > NH3 (2◦ > 3◦ > 1◦).
  • Hydrazine Trap: NH2 − NH2 is weaker than NH3 due to −I effect.
  • Benzylamine vs Aniline: PhCH2NH2 (pKb = 4.70) is an aliphatic-like base, far stronger than PhNH2 (pKb = 9.38).

trapCards.title: Trap 3: Hinsberg, Carbylamine & HNO<sub>2</sub> Distinc- tions
trapCards.html:
• Hinsberg (PhSO2Cl): – 1◦ amine → alkali-soluble solid. – 2◦ amine → alkali-insoluble solid. – 3◦ amine → no reaction (clear/unreacted). – Amides (−CONH2) and urea do not give Hinsberg amine test.
  • Carbylamine (CHCl3/KOH): Given by both aliphatic & aromatic 1◦ amines; 2◦/3◦ fail.
  • HNO2 on 3◦ Arylamines: Gives p-nitroso-C- substitution (not N-nitroso).

trapCards.title: Trap 4: Diazonium Salts & Aniline EAS Anomalies
trapCards.html:
• Ethanol Reduction: ArN+2 Cl− + EtOH → ArH + CH3CHO (deamination, never ArOEt!).
  • Nitration of Aniline: Gives 47% m-nitroaniline via −NH+3 ; protect with Ac2O first for pure p-isomer.
  • Friedel–Crafts: Aniline forms a salt with AlCl3 =⇒ no FC alkylation/acylation.
  • Storage Colour: Arylamines darken by atmospheric oxidation (not reduction).
  • Sulfanilic Acid: Contains N + S =⇒ blood-red Las- saigne’s test.

constantsHtml:
• High-Yield NTA JEE Main 2023–2026 Exam Intelligence (88 PYQs: 75 MCQs + 13 Section B)
  • Biomolecules is one of the highest-ROI chapters in Organic Chemistry, consistently contributing 1–2 questions per
  • shift (4–8 marks) with minimal calculation overhead. Across 2023–2026 papers, over 85% of questions cluster around five
  • NCERT pillars: (1) Carbohydrates (glucose/fructose open-chain vs cyclic Haworth/Fischer structures, D/L configuration,
  • anomers vs epimers, reducing vs non-reducing disaccharides, glycosidic linkages in sucrose/maltose/lactose/starch/cellulose),
  • (2) Amino Acids (essential list, one-letter codes, S-containing & heterocyclic side chains, zwitterion/pH/pI behaviour),
  • (3) Peptides & Proteins (peptide bond count n − 1, sequence permutations, 1°/2°/3° structures, denaturation, Bi-
  • uret/Ninhydrin tests), (4) Nucleic Acids (purine/pyrimidine structures, DNA vs RNA, Chargaff’s rule, H-bond counting,

formulaCards.title: 1. Carbohydrates: Monosaccharides & Glucose Re- actions
formulaCards.html:
• D/L Notation: Determined by the lowest asymmetric carbon (−OH on right in Fischer ⇒ D; on left ⇒ L, correlated to D-(+)-glyceraldehyde).
  • D-(+)-Glucose vs D-(-)-Fructose: Both have the same configuration at C3, C4, C5 (3 chiral centres in open-chain fructose; 4 in open-chain glucose; 5 in cyclic pyranose/furanose).
  • Key Reactions of D-Glucose (C6H12O6): – HI, ∆ −→ n-hexane (proves straight 6-C chain). – NH2OH −→ Glucoxime; HCN −→ Cyanohydrin (proves > C = O). – Br2-H2O (mild) −→ Gluconic acid (proves −CHO). – Conc. HNO3 (strong) −→ Saccharic acid (dicar- boxylic acid; proves primary −CH2OH). – Ac2O (excess) −→ Glucose pentaacetate (proves 5 −OH groups). – NaBH4 −→ Sorbitol (glucitol). – Negative Tests for Glucose / Pentaacetate: Glucose does not give Schiff’s test, NaHSO3 adduct, or 2,4-DNP test (aldehyde is locked in cyclic hemi- acetal). Glucose pentaacetate does not react with NH2OH or 2,4-DNP (no free −OH at C1 to open ring).
  • Anomers (C1 in aldoses, C2 in ketoses): α-D- (+)-glucose ([α]D = +112◦, m.p. 419 K, crystallised at 303 K) and β-D-(+)-glucose ([α]D = +19◦, m.p. 423 K, crystallised at 371 K) equilibrate in water to +52.5◦ (mutarotation).
  • Epimers: Differ at a single chiral centre other than anomeric C (e.g., D-glucose & D-mannose at C2; D-glucose & D-galactose at C4).

formulaCards.title: 2. Reducing Sugars, Disaccharides & Polysaccha- rides
formulaCards.html:
• Reducing Sugars: Have a free hemiacetal/hemiketal −OH at the anomeric carbon; reduce Tollens’, Fehling’s, and Benedict’s reagents. Includes all monosaccharides (including fructose, which tautomerises via enediol in base to glucose/mannose) and maltose, lactose.
  • Non-Reducing Sugars: Anomeric carbons locked in ac- etal/ketal glycosidic bond. Examples: Sucrose, trehalose, and polysaccharides (starch, cellulose, glycogen).
  • Disaccharide Linkages & Hydrolysis: – Sucrose (Invert Sugar): α-D-glucose (C1) ↔ β- D-fructose (C2). Dextrorotatory (+66.5◦); hydroly- sis (invertase / H+) gives equimolar D-(+)-glucose (+52.5◦) + D-(-)-fructose (−92.4◦) ⇒ net laevoro- tatory (−39.9◦). – Maltose: α-D-glucose (C1) → α-D-glucose (C4) (α- 1,4 linkage). – Lactose (Milk sugar): β-D-galactose (C1) → β- D-glucose (C4) (β-1,4 linkage).
  • Polysaccharides: – Starch: Amylose (15–20%, water-soluble, linear α-1,4-D-glucose) + Amylopectin (80–85%, water- insoluble, branched α-1,4 & α-1,6). – Glycogen: Animal starch; structure like amy- lopectin but more highly branched. – Cellulose: Linear polymer of β-D-glucose (β-1,4 linkage); plant cell walls.
  • Carbohydrate Tests: Molisch’s test (all carbohy- drates, violet ring); Seliwanoff’s test (ketoses react faster than aldoses via dehydration to furfural/HMF).

formulaCards.title: 3. Amino Acids: Classification, Codes & Isoelectric Point
formulaCards.html:
• Essential Amino Acids (10 — Mnemonic: PVT TIM HALL): Phenylalanine (F), Valine (V), Threonine (T), Tryptophan (W), Isoleucine (I), Methionine (M), Histidine (H), Arginine (R), Leucine (L), Lysine (K). (Arg & His are semi-essential; Gly, Ala, Ser, Cys, Tyr, Asp, Glu, Asn, Gln, Pro are non-essential.)
  • Key One-Letter Codes: Aspartic acid (D), Glutamic acid (E), Asparagine (N), Glutamine (Q), Arginine (R), Lysine (K), Phenylalanine (F), Tyrosine (Y), Tryptophan (W).
  • Special Side Chains: – Achiral: Glycine (H2N − CH2 − COOH, only opti- cally inactive α-AA). – Two Chiral Centres: Isoleucine (Ile) and Threo- nine (Thr). – Sulphur-containing: Cysteine (−CH2SH, dimerises to cystine −S − S−) and Methionine (−CH2CH2SCH3). – Phenolic (neutral FeCl3 violet): Tyrosine (−CH2C6H4OH). – Alcoholic (CAN test): Serine (−CH2OH), Thre- onine. – Amide (Hofmann bromamide): Glutamine, As- paragine. – Cyclic (5-membered): Proline (2◦ amine); Het- erocyclic: Histidine, Tryptophan, Proline.
  • Zwitterion & pI: At pH < pI ⇒ Cationic (H3N+ − CHR − COOH); at pH > pI ⇒ An- ionic (H2N − CHR − COO−). For neutral AAs, pI = pKa1+pKa2 . 2

formulaCards.title: 4. Peptides, Proteins, Enzymes & Denaturation
formulaCards.html:
• Peptide Linkage (−CO − NH−): A linear polypeptide of n amino acids has n − 1 peptide bonds. Number of sequences from n distinct AAs (each used once) = n!; with repetition from k AAs for length n = kn.
  • Protein Structure Levels: – 1◦ (Primary): Specific sequence of α-amino acids (covalent peptide bonds). – 2◦ (Secondary): α-helix & β-pleated sheet (sta- bilised by H-bonding). – 3◦ (Tertiary): Overall 3D folding (H-bonds, disul- phide −S − S−, van der Waals, electrostatic forces; forms fibrous/globular). – 4◦ (Quaternary): Spatial arrangement of ≥ 2 polypeptide subunits.
  • Denaturation: Heat or pH change destroys 2◦, 3◦, 4◦ structures and biological activity (e.g., coagulation of egg white), while primary (1◦) structure remains intact.
  • Tests: Biuret test (violet colour for ≥ 2 peptide bonds: tripeptides+, biuret; negative for free AAs & dipeptides). Ninhydrin test (blue-violet for α-amino acids/proteins).
  • Enzymes: Globular proteins; highly specific biocatalysts that lower Ea (Invertase: sucrose → glu+fru; Zymase: glu- cose → ethanol + CO2; Diastase: starch → maltose; Mal- tase: maltose → glucose; Pepsin: proteins → AAs; Urease: urea hydrolysis, found in soyabean).
